To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have produced and characterized two monoclonal antibodies against heparan proteoglycan, and that these mAbs react with normal basement membranes, and with basement membrane abnormalities in human kidney biopsied from patients with various forms of glomerular disease.
mAbs to HSPG can be produced and that these mAbs can be used to study normal and abnormal human tissues.

1) we have prepared and characterized two mAbs that react specifically with HSPG; 2) these mAbs stain BM of all organs in normal tissue in a pattern typical of BM HSPG; and 3) the mAbs stain GBM and other BM in a variety of pathologic kidney conditions, and provide information about the distribution of HSPC in these diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of mAbs to HSPG.
the development and application of a new class of monoclonal antibodies to basement membrane HSPG.
the development of a series of monoclonal antibodies (MAbs) to heparan sulphate proteoglycan, and their application to the study normal human tissue and pathologic renal biopsies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mAbs to HSPG recognize the HSPG core, and that they react with BM in a pattern typical of HSPGs.
mAbs to HSPG can be useful in the evaluation of glomeruloneprhitis and in the understanding of the mechanisms underlying glomerulonepohritis and other renal disease.
the monoclonal antibodies to HSPG are a very useful tool to study the distribution of HSPGs in the basement membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mAbs to HSPG may be useful tools to study the structure and function of the GBM, and the pathogenesis of diseases of the GBM.
the use of monoclonal antibodies against heparan sulphate proteoglycans in the study of normal and pathologic human renal biopsies has been developed.
the mAbs react with the core protein of HSPG and recognize HSPG in a wide variety of normal and pathological human and bovine tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mAbs are specific for the HSPG core proteins.
the use of mAb's against HSPG can be used to detect the presence and absence of this molecule in the GBM.
the HSPG is an important component of GBM and other basement membranes and that its distribution in the GBM is altered in a variety of glomerulopathies.
